THING.description: root: any node type is-a THING

METHOD.description: a named modeling approach/theory/law/model (e.g. μ(I) rheology, kinetic theory, NGF, DEM, RFT)

PARAMETER.description: a named physical quantity/constant/coefficient in equations (e.g. μ, I, d, P, τ, g, ρ_s, T, A, ξ, μ_s, b)

PHENOMENON.description: a physical effect/behavior methods capture (e.g. nonlocal creep, thin-body strengthening, secondary rheology, segregation, clogging)

PROPERTY.description: a generic physical property/quantity not fitting the above (kept for residual cases)

constitutive_law.description: a constitutive law relating output quantity/quantities to >=1 input quantity (n-ary)
constitutive_law.semantic_boundary: a FORMAL/QUANTITATIVE law output=f(inputs+params), stated as a formula or explicit functional relation. NOT a prose 'X depends on Y' (that is influences), NOT a definition (defines), NOT a measurement setup (measures).

influences.description: one quantity influences / depends on >=1 target quantity (n-ary, general dependence)
influences.semantic_boundary: X functionally depends on / varies with Y (a genuine causal or scaling dependence). NOT a co-listing of parallel items (composed_of), NOT a classification (defines), NOT 'we tested X' (measures), NOT 'X is part of Y' (composed_of).

defines.description: one entity is defined-as / identified-with / named-by another (definitional identity, n-ary)
defines.semantic_boundary: a DEFINITIONAL identity: X is defined as / is / denotes / is named / is classified into Y. NOT a structural part-of (composed_of), NOT a functional dependence (influences). 'X is analogous to Y' is a CLAIM not a definition.

composed_of.description: one whole is composed-of / part-of >=1 component (n-ary composition)
composed_of.semantic_boundary: STRUCTURAL composition: parts that make up a whole (model A = B + C). NOT classification (defines), NOT 'X has control params' (influences), NOT experimental setup description, NOT 'we tested X by doing Y'.

measures.description: a quantity is measured by / characterizes >=1 measure
measures.semantic_boundary: a measurement/evaluation relation: X is measured/evaluated by instrument/method Y. NOT a functional law (constitutive_law), NOT a dependence (influences).

claim_relation.semantic_boundary: a DISCOURSE relation between claims/findings (supports/contrasts/outperforms). NOT a method-to-method development (extends/improves/compares — those are evolution), NOT a measurement (measures).

extends.semantic_boundary: X GENERALIZES Y (X extends Y's scope/regime/params; X is a direct technical extension of Y). NOT improves (X need not be more accurate, just broader), NOT background (X is a direct technical inheritance, not a motivation citation), NOT claim_relation (this is method-to-method).

improves.description: X improves Y's accuracy/applicability, resolving Y's limitation
improves.semantic_boundary: X RESOLVES a limitation of Y (X is more accurate/applicable BECAUSE it fixes something Y fails at; first-principles vs phenomenological = improves). NOT compares (X is NOT a parallel different-mechanism alternative; X builds on Y and is better), NOT extends (X is better not just broader).

compares.semantic_boundary: A and B are put side by side: either (i) PARALLEL different-mechanism alternatives with overlapping scope (both model the same phenomenon, different assumptions), or (ii) THEORY-vs-EXPERIMENT / prediction-vs-observation validation ('data compared with predictions', 'simulations agree with experiments', 'in contrast with'), or (iii) equivalence/contrast of formulations ('equivalent', 'the same as', 'rather than'). NOT improves (neither fixes the other's limitation), NOT extends (neither generalizes the other).

replaces.semantic_boundary: X SUBSTITUTES Y outright (X is used INSTEAD of Y; Y is retired). NOT improves (replaces = Y is gone, improves = Y still used + X better).

adapts.description: X adapts Y to a new scenario
adapts.semantic_boundary: X PORTS Y to a NEW scenario/regime/domain Y wasn't designed for (adaptation of Y's mechanism). NOT extends (adapts = new scenario, extends = broader scope within same setting).

background.semantic_boundary: X cites Y as MOTIVATION/prior context only (Y inspired X but X is NOT a direct technical extension/inheritance of Y). NOT extends (no direct technical lineage), NOT improves (no limitation fix).

visualizes.description: X is made visible/observable by Y (an imaging/visualization relation where an instrument or technique renders a phenomenon/property observable).
visualizes.semantic_boundary: Use only when a method/technique makes a phenomenon observable; not for mere measurement, detection, or data collection without direct visualization.

configured_by.description: X is configured/controlled by Y (a setup relation where a device or system's parameter is set by a component or condition).
configured_by.semantic_boundary: Use when one entity actively sets or controls another’s parameter; NOT for mere association, ownership, or one-way dependency without explicit configuration action.

transitions_to_state.description: X transitions to state Y under condition Z (a phase-transition/state-change relation where a system enters a new state when a parameter crosses a threshold).
transitions_to_state.semantic_boundary: Use when a system changes state due to a threshold-crossing parameter; not for mere correlation, causation, or static co-occurrence.

absence_of_phenomenon.description: A phenomenon or effect is explicitly absent or not observed in a system (e.g., no shear localization, no dependence).
absence_of_phenomenon.semantic_boundary: Use this pattern only when a phenomenon is explicitly stated as absent or not observed; do not use for mere non-mention, absence of a thing, or a negative correlation.

statistical_comparison.description: A comparison between observed data and a null/control/shuffled baseline to establish statistical significance or distinguish signal from noise.
statistical_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use for explicit comparisons against a null, control, or shuffled baseline; NOT for simple correlations, differences between groups, or descriptive statistics.

agrees_with.description: X is in agreement with / consistent with Y (a validation relation where findings or observations align with prior work or predictions).
agrees_with.semantic_boundary: Use when one finding explicitly supports or matches another claim or prediction, not when they merely co-occur, are compared, or one causes the other.

learns_about.description: X learns about / optimizes for target Y while following/using behavior Z (a learning-target vs behavior-distribution distinction)
learns_about.semantic_boundary: Use when the learner explicitly optimizes for a target while constrained by a behavior; not for mere co-occurrence, causation, or the behavior being the target itself.

has_advantage_over.description: X has advantages over Y (a comparative evaluation of benefits, distinct from improves which implies fixing limitations)
has_advantage_over.semantic_boundary: Use when explicitly comparing benefits of X over Y, not when X fixes Y’s flaws (improves) or when X merely outperforms Y in a task (better_than).

validates_against.description: X is validated/verified by comparing against Y (a reference, standard, or expected result)
validates_against.semantic_boundary: Use when X is checked against Y as a standard or expected result; not when X merely depends on Y or when X and Y are co-listed.

equivalent_formulation.description: Two formulations/models are shown to be mathematically equivalent or interchangeable (same predictive content, different notational/derivational form).
equivalent_formulation.semantic_boundary: Equivalent formulation applies when two methods are proven interchangeable, not when they merely coexist or one is a special case of the other.

describes.description: X describes Y (a theory/model/approach provides a description or account of a phenomenon or process)
describes.semantic_boundary: describes applies when X is a method/approach explicitly offering an account of Y, not when X merely mentions, uses, or evaluates Y.

functional_identity.description: Two functions/expressions are shown to be equal or identical in form (e.g., C(x,N) = G(x,N) + 1/2).
functional_identity.semantic_boundary: Use when two expressions are explicitly equated as identical forms; NOT for causal links, definitions, or mere co-occurrence of variables.

validates.description: X validates/confirms Y by comparison (theory vs experiment, calculated vs measured) — a verification relation where one entity is checked against another as ground truth
validates.semantic_boundary: Use when one property is explicitly checked against another as ground truth; not for mere co-occurrence, correlation, or a stated equality without verification intent.

predicts.description: X (a model/method) predicts Y (a distribution/outcome) under conditions Z — a predictive relation where a model generates predictions for a system
predicts.semantic_boundary: Use when a model/method outputs a predicted quantity for a system under specified conditions; NOT for observed correlations, causal claims, or mere co-occurrence of variables.

shares_similarity.description: X shares similarities with Y but differs in specific aspects (a partial overlap/analogy relation between formulations/models).
shares_similarity.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly compared to another with stated overlap and difference; not for equivalence, contradiction, or mere co-occurrence.
